learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and use of the principles of circuit theory and electrical machines.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enable the learning of new methods and theories, and provide versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Analyze and solve basic electrical circuits, direct and alternating current, containing passive elements.
Know how to use the main electrical measurement devices (multimeter, wattmeter, oscilloscope, etc.).
Select an electrical machine based on energy transformation needs.
Perform, with a certain skill, the electrical assembly of a circuit or electrical machine.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1: Elements of an electrical circuit
Topic 3: Single-phase alternating current electrical circuits
Topic 4: Power in single-phase AC electrical circuits
Topic 5: Three-phase alternating current electrical circuits
Topic 8: Asynchronous alternating current electrical machines
assessment_rules: The course can be evaluated via two modalities: a mixed system or a simple system. System I (Mixed) consists of: Laboratory practices (20% with a minimum score of 5/10 in each of 5 practices), a Partial test (20%), Theoretical-practical exercises (10%), and a Final written test (50% with a minimum score of 4.5/10; this test has theoretical and practical parts, requiring a minimum of 4/10 in each to average). System II (Simple) is based exclusively on a global final test comprising two parts: a Written final test (80% with a minimum of 5/10; requiring 4/10 in each part to average) and a Practical exam (20% with a minimum of 5/10). The use of unpermitted materials or electronic devices during evaluation may result in a grade of '0' and potential disciplinary action.
